This led to some minor dovish repricing but today's beat in Eurozone core inflation will keep the September meeting live.

The Fed left interest rates unchanged with three dissenters voting for a hike.

The consensus was that Fed's Logan and Fed's Hammack would prefer a rate increase, but we also got Fed's Kashkari joining the dissenting camp.

I guess the fact that Fed's Kashkari is a hawkish member, combined with the roughly 30% probability of a rate hike that was priced in before the release, led to some dovish repricing, even though nothing has changed in the bigger picture.

Fed Chair Warsh didn't offer any clues about the next meeting as he continues to limit forward guidance.

How sticky is inflation? Let's see: Prior +3.0% HICP +2.9% vs +2.8% y/y expected Prior +3.0% Italy's preliminary inflation data for July ticked slightly higher.

According to the preliminary estimate, Italy's headline CPI rose 2.8% year-on-year in July, matching market expectations and slowing from the previous 3.0% pace.

The harmonized measure of inflation (HICP), which is used by the ECB to compare price developments across the euro area, increased 2.9% year-on-year, slightly above the 2.8% consensus forecast but down from the prior 3.0% reading.

From a broader perspective, the data is unlikely to materially alter expectations for ECB policy, especially after the Eurozone Core CPI Y/Y beat expectations coming at 2.5% vs 2.4% expected.

This will keep expectations for a rate hike in September alive.

This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.
